CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Palopo.
2. Mayor is the Mayor of Palopo.
3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government which is the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives Institution of Palopo City which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Palopo City.
6. Regional Agency is the Regional Apparatus of Palopo City which includes the Regional Secretariat, Secretariat of the Regional House of Representatives, Regional Offices and Regional Technical Institutions.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those still in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence which include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict and the State.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or can result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
17. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from the aspects of health, education and economic independence.
26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PALOPO CITY
NUMBER 5 YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household as well as outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, among others Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection.
prioritizing the Implementation of Regional Government in the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as regulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government. The Basic Services referred to, one of which is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.
On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps in order to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community especially to women and children. The causes include among others the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence to answer while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from actions to prevent acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society.
Our hope is that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

5.3.rationale: The Indonesian text does mention "lembaga adat" (customary institutions) in the definition of "Penyelenggara" (Pasal 1 angka 13) and in the elucidation of Pasal 18 (Ayat (1) huruf d) listing non-government actors including "lembaga adat" and "tokoh adat". However, this is only an inclusion in a list/definition of possible actors for cooperation/implementation, not an explicit requirement or described mechanism of engaging traditional/cultural institutions in program design/implementation. If the indicator requires active/explicit traditional/cultural engagement, the judge over-interpreted mere mention as engagement (evaluation failure). At the same time, if the rubric counts naming customary institutions as implementers/partners as sufficient ‘engagement’, then the golden label "No" would be wrong; given the text explicitly includes customary institutions, the golden label is at least questionable.

18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from the aspects of health, education and economic independence.
26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

This is an explicit inclusion of crisis/conflict settings within the scope of who is covered. Although "perlindungan khusus" (Pasal 1 angka 11) is defined only for children, the indicator is about women in crisis settings; the policy still explicitly recognizes victims (including women) in conflict/post-conflict contexts. Since this relevant information was present in the retrieved candidates (Article 1 definition) and supports a "Yes" for coverage of women in crisis settings, the golden label "Yes" aligns with the text and the judge’s "No" appears to be an overly strict interpretation; however because the discrepancy is golden Yes vs predicted No, the main issue is that the judge treated the indicator as requiring special measures rather than explicit inclusion/coverage. Given the golden label is Yes and the text supports at least inclusion, the golden label seems correct and the judge’s No is not; thus this is best categorized as a golden-label-consistent case where the judge erred. But since root-cause options do not include 'judge error only' without evidence, we classify as golden_label_issue only if judge correct; here judge is not correct.
